body:
## Objective

Determine whether binary RTCP XR (RFC 3611) support belongs in `rfc6035-2otel`, a sibling receiver, or neither, using real/testable implementations and a concrete transport/security design. This issue is research and design only; it does not authorize quietly adding a second network protocol to the released RFC 6035 collector.

## Questions answered

- Maintained real implementations: PJSIP/PJMEDIA and Jitsi/libjitsi; Pion RTCP is the preferred Go decoder and fixture generator; Wireshark is the independent wire oracle.
- Real capture: PJSIP's upstream two-UA XR test produces a peer exchange and is the first bounded capture source.
- Transport: passive PCAP/AF_PACKET on TAP/SPAN, initially offline; no generic direct listener and no production listener change.
- Identity: only a configured bounded capture-sensor/source registry becomes a metric dimension; SSRC, tuple and correlation detail remain in logs.
- Signals: normalize under a distinct `rtcp.xr.*` contract; do not mix protocol populations or invent RFC 6035 side/one-way semantics.
- Repository boundary: a sibling `rtcp-xr-2otel`, because media-plane negotiation, capture privilege, binary parsing and SRTCP materially change the threat and lifecycle boundary.
- Validation: PJSIP real capture plus Pion boundary/sentinel fixture, cross-checked in Wireshark, then fuzzed offline before any privileged capture helper.

## Decision

Build a sibling receiver after the bounded PoC. Do not integrate binary RTCP-XR into `rfc6035-2otel`.

## Acceptance

- [x] Current upstream documentation/source identifies at least two usable RFC 3611 implementations or one implementation plus a standards-grade packet generator.
- [x] A recommended architecture names repository boundary, UDP/RTCP ownership, identity model and signal mapping.
- [x] Security and cardinality risks are explicit.
- [x] A bounded proof-of-concept test plan identifies how to capture and validate a real emitted packet without changing production deployment.
- [x] The issue closes with one decision: integrate here, build a sibling receiver, or defer with precise missing evidence.

comments.body:
Research decision: **build a sibling `rtcp-xr-2otel`; do not add binary RTCP-XR to this SIP/PUBLISH collector.**

Current implementation evidence:

- PJSIP/PJMEDIA commit `5b0894b8a72a67e4931f5da20aacc7fcabc6ba21` has the real BT=7 VoIP Metrics block builder and an upstream two-UA XR exchange test (`tests/pjsua/scripts-call/415_call_rtcp_xr.py`).
- Pion RTCP v1.2.17/current commit `e6362230ba763b2807a1a99e620f0a2fd05dda71` provides typed BT=7 marshal/unmarshal and a round-trip fixture generator suitable for the Go decoder.
- Jitsi/libjitsi commit `6c95bf2236610e0d2c47109a73501b2078963f9f` independently serializes and inserts XR into outgoing RTCP.
- Wireshark commit `27a642453b370e9e14c566bdf269b4872d966e2f` independently validates PT=207, BT=7, block length=8.

Transport and security boundary:

- RFC 6035 here is signaling-plane SIP PUBLISH over one configured UDP listener. RFC 3611 is media-plane binary RTCP, normally sent to the media peer and often protected by SRTCP.
- A generic direct UDP listener would not receive negotiated peer RTCP without owning SDP/ICE/NAT/port lifecycle. `rtcp-mux` changes demultiplexing, not session ownership.
- The sibling should start as an offline PCAP decoder, then use a narrowly privileged capture helper on TAP/SPAN/AF_PACKET with an unprivileged decoder. The PoC must not accept SRTCP keys or change production listeners.
- Metrics use only a configured bounded capture-sensor/source registry. SSRCs, five-tuples, capture interface and correlation details stay in logs. SIP Call-ID correlation is a separate TTL-bounded mapping problem and not PoC scope.
- Raw fixed-point and sentinel semantics remain under a distinct `rtcp.xr.*` contract; they must not be mixed into `rfc6035.call.*` or invent `report.side`/one-way-delay equivalence.

Bounded proof:

1. Build PJSIP with `PJMEDIA_HAS_RTCP_XR=1`, run the upstream two-UA `--rtcp-xr` test, and capture only the isolated test interface.
2. Prove PT=207, BT=7, length=8 in Wireshark/tshark and compare with PJSIP call-quality output.
3. Generate a separate Pion v1.2.17 boundary/sentinel fixture programmatically.
4. Decode both fixtures in a new sibling offline-PCAP prototype and compare its normalized output with Pion/Wireshark.
5. Fuzz RTCP and PCAP framing, truncation, declared lengths, padding, compound packets, sentinel/range handling and mux ambiguity before considering privileged capture.

Linphone remains the separate practical non-Poly RFC 6035 compatibility sender; generic RTCP-XR support in PJSIP/Jitsi is not evidence that either emits RFC 6035 SIP PUBLISH.

title: Design: assess binary RFC 3611 RTCP-XR receiver support

body:
## Mission

Turn the existing generated RFC 6035 signal inventory into one operational Grafana Dashboard v2 resource on the m7kni stack, publish and reconcile it through the established `gc-gitsync-m7kni` GitSync path, publish the generated alert rules, and apply proportionate GitHub Actions hardening found by a full zizmor auditor-persona review.

This is a single-dashboard delivery. Dashboard identity remains `rfc6035-2otel`; the GitSync destination is `networking/rfc6035-2otel.json`; the live folder is the existing GitSync-managed `networking` folder.

## Binding design

### Dashboard v2 and dynamic layout

- Emit `apiVersion: dashboard.grafana.app/v2`, `kind: Dashboard`, `metadata.name: rfc6035-2otel`.
- Use Dashboard v2 `elements` plus a top-level `TabsLayout`.
- Tabs: **Operations**, **Call quality**, **Raw reports**, **Diagnostics**, **Collector**.
- Use conditional rendering for optional/event-driven signals. One-way delay is visible only when its series exists; its absence remains normal.
- Preserve a single generated source of truth; do not hand-edit the generated JSON in GitSync.

### Variables and data sources

- Datasource variables default to `grafanacloud-prom` and `grafanacloud-logs`.
- `site` is `service_instance_id`, multi/all, sourced from released collector report metrics.
- `sender` is `rfc6035_sender_name`, multi/all, filtered by selected site.
- All metric and log queries scope to site/sender where applicable.

### Sparse-event query contract

RFC 6035 histograms receive one observation per completed call, not continuous samples. Every quality query must be guarded by a positive count/report increase in the selected window so an empty interval cannot render as catastrophic zero quality. Use `$__range` for selected-window operational summaries; use an event-presence guard with any trend window.

### Operational story

- Operations: reports in range, reporting handsets, mean/p95 MOS, p95 loss, p95 RTT/jitter, unknown sender reports, export failures.
- Call quality: per-site/per-handset quality trends and breakdowns with correct units and decision-oriented legends.
- Raw reports: a Loki panel using the verified `rfc6035.report.received` metadata filters.
- Metric data links open the Raw reports tab using `dtab=Raw-Reports`, preserving `${__url_time_range}` and applying clicked site/sender values.
- Diagnostics: R-factor, discard rate, dialect/side/jitter detail, optional one-way delay.
- Collector: expose all nine bounded self-observability instruments, while treating event-only absent series as no events rather than broken collection.

### Publication and reconciliation

- Add `grafana-sync.yml` following the existing 2otel pattern.
- Dashboard path: commit generated v2 JSON to `rknightion/gc-gitsync-m7kni` at `networking/rfc6035-2otel.json` with an explicit pathspec, then verify Grafana applied the exact GitSync commit.
- Use the provisioned broker contract `permission-set: gitsync`, `role: gitsync-rfc6035-2otel`; never fall back to `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- Publish alert resources with `gcx resources push`, prune only the RFC 6035 rule folder before push, then read back the resources.
- Pin every action to a full SHA and verify the installed gcx archive checksum.
- Preserve current shared publication behavior: docs/test-only main pushes may publish edge/main images; no path-filter change.

### Alerts and recording rules

- Convert generated rules to App Platform `AlertRule` resources and link them to dashboard/panels.
- Keep high packet loss and export failure rules, add unknown-sender reporting, and validate expressions against live data without manufacturing a firing incident.
- Alerts remain absence-safe and low-volume-aware.
- Recording rules were assessed and rejected for now: current data is tiny/low-cardinality and important aggregations depend on the selected dashboard time range. Fixed-window recorded series would add semantic/storage cost without useful acceleration.

### Actions hardening

- Add top-level `permissions: {}` to docs sync.
- Add clear job names and explanatory permission comments where useful.
- Add safe same-ref concurrency to Docker Security, Scorecard and zizmor; do not cancel publication workflows mid-write.
- Upgrade the zizmor tool input to 1.29.0 and apply the pending distroless digest update.
- Keep the four `secrets-outside-env` findings as an explicit accepted advisory: the two values are broker identifiers, not bearer tokens, and a real fix requires a shared GitHub Environments policy and secret migration.
- Do not make low-value cosmetic auditor findings release-blocking.

## External prerequisites to prove before implementation closes

- `TS_WIF_CLIENT_ID` and `TS_WIF_AUDIENCE` exist (already observed).
- The repository-specific OpenBao role `gitsync-rfc6035-2otel` exists and can mint a token; do not assume it from sibling state.
- `GRAFANA_SERVER`, `GRAFANA_STACK_ID`, and `GRAFANA_TOKEN` are available for CI rule publication, or document the exact provisioning boundary if absent.
- The alert folder exists and the GitHub-push service account has Admin on that folder before pushing rules.

## Acceptance

- [x] Generator emits one valid Dashboard v2 manifest with the five approved tabs and stable identity.
- [x] Prometheus/Loki datasource, site and sender variables default and resolve correctly on m7kni.
- [x] Quality queries return live named-handset results and no false zero during empty windows.
- [x] Raw report panel returns live rows; metric drilldowns preserve time/site/sender and open the Raw reports tab.
- [x] Diagnostics conditionally handles one-way-delay absence.
- [x] Collector tab covers all nine bounded self-observability instruments.
- [x] Generated dashboard and rule drift tests pass; missing fixtures/resources fail rather than skip.
- [ ] Dashboard GitSync action pushes/reconciles the explicit destination and proves Grafana applied it.
- [x] Alert resources validate, publish, read back, and remain absence-safe.
- [ ] A full dashboard snapshot is visually inspected and at least one real iteration is made if it reveals a defect.
- [x] Zizmor regular audit passes; the auditor-persona result is dispositioned with no hidden findings.
- [x] Local `make check` and exact-head CI/security workflows pass.
- [x] Durable issue comments name all external side effects and any external prerequisite not provisioned.

## Non-goals

- No second dashboard.
- No Helm-provider test.
- No Grafana recording rules unless measured query cost disproves the current decision.
- No RFC 3611 binary receiver in this issue; that is a separate protocol-boundary design because it changes transport, threat model and parser surface.

body:
## What

Use **AAISP's special dialling codes** as an on-demand generator of real voice-quality reports, to
replace and extend fixtures that are currently synthetic.

## Why

`vq-collector`'s README carries this caveat, and it has carried over to this project: **the test
samples are built from the RFC 6035 / RFC 3611 examples, not from a wire capture.** A parser validated
only against the spec's own examples is validated against the spec, not against what Poly actually
emits.

AAISP publishes special codes that terminate on their platform, so a call can be placed and held for a
known duration, with known audio, at zero cost and without involving another person. That turns
"wait for a real call to happen" into a repeatable test.

## The codes

| Code | Effect | Use here |
|---|---|---|
| `*103` | Play hold music | **Best sample generator** — long, continuous, known audio. Hold for a defined duration to get a full `VQSessionReport` with realistic jitter/loss/MOS |
| `*100` | 1 kHz tone test | Constant-bitrate reference; the cleanest possible signal, useful as a control |
| `*105` | Read the time | Short call — exercises short-duration reports |
| `*400`–`*699` | **Return a specific SIP error code** | Failure-path coverage: what does the handset publish, if anything, when a call fails at a defined point? |
| `*104` / `17070` | Read back calling number | Trivial short call |

`*400`–`*699` is the interesting one beyond sample generation: it makes SIP failure modes reproducible
on demand, so the collector's behaviour on reports from failed and very short calls can be tested
deliberately rather than waiting for one to occur naturally.

## Scope

- A documented procedure (not necessarily automated) for generating reports on demand: which code,
  how long to hold, what to expect.
- Diff a captured real report against the existing synthetic fixtures and **record the differences**.
  Any divergence is a parser bug or a fixture bug; both matter.
- Extend fixtures with real captures, keeping the synthetic ones as spec-conformance cases. Label
  which is which — this distinction is the entire point.
- Cover the short-call and failed-call cases surfaced by `*400`–`*699`.

## ✅ Dialect coverage is FINE — an earlier version of this issue said otherwise and was WRONG

This issue originally claimed `PHONE-B` had never delivered a report and blamed a shadowed firewall
rule. **Both halves were wrong.** Corrected 2026-08-13, kept here so nobody re-derives it:

- **Both dialects are arriving and parsing correctly.** From the live collector log:
  `source=IP-PHONE-A:5060 dialect=standard` and `source=IP-PHONE-B:5060 dialect=prestandard`,
  repeatedly, on 2026-08-13. The deliberate split across the two handsets is working exactly as
  intended.
- **The wrong-evidence trap:** the "zero reports from PHONE-B" finding came from querying
  `{service_name="syslog"} | appname="vqcollector"` in Loki. That is the **retired** `vq-collector`'s
  syslog stream. `rfc6035-2otel` replaced it and exports OTLP directly, so it writes nothing there —
  an empty result was inevitable and meant nothing. **Check `docker logs rfc6035-2otel` or the OTLP
  data, never the old collector's stream.**
- **The firewall was never blocking it.** The rule `[IOT] Allow -> vq-collector (HOST-A:5060)` was
  genuinely mis-sequenced (seq 1201, below the seq-336 catch-all block, same `prio_group`), so it was
  passing nothing — but the traffic was already permitted by the multi-interface
  `Allow -> syslog (HOST-A:514)` rule at `prio_group` 200000, whose `syslog_ports` alias contains
  **514 and 5060**. Shadowed, but with no consequence.

So this issue is about **fixture quality**, not about unblocking a dead path. The real gap stands:
the pre-standard grammar was built from measurement rather than a specification, and both dialects'
fixtures should be checked against captures generated deliberately rather than opportunistically.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `PHONE-B`'s reports confirmed arriving (firewall rule corrected to sequence below 336)
- [ ] At least one real report captured per dialect via `*103`
- [ ] Real captures diffed against the synthetic fixtures, differences documented
- [ ] Fixtures extended with real captures, clearly labelled real vs synthetic
- [ ] Short-call and failed-call behaviour covered using `*105` and `*400`–`*699`
- [ ] Procedure written up in `docs/` so it can be repeated
title: Use AAISP special codes (*103, *100, *400-*699) to generate real VQ reports and replace synthetic fixtures

## Defect

The released v0.1.0 instrument `rfc6035_2otel.build_info` is an observable gauge with explicit OpenTelemetry unit `1`. Grafana Cloud Prometheus compatibility translates that unit on a gauge to the live series `rfc6035_2otel_build_info_ratio`.

The frozen Wave 2 contract and generated consumers require the exact Prometheus name `rfc6035_2otel_build_info`. This is live gate evidence, not a catalog prediction.

## Narrow repair

- create the build-info observable gauge without an explicit SDK unit, matching the sibling implementation
- retain gauge value 1 and the four frozen build attributes
- retain the catalog description of the value as dimensionless
- add a focused regression assertion for the emitted SDK metadata
- regenerate only if the catalog-driven artifacts change

## Acceptance

- focused self-observability tests pass
- `make check` passes
- exact-head CI passes
- a patch release is published by CI and deployed to HOST-A by digest
- live query filtered on the patch `service_version` returns `rfc6035_2otel_build_info` and no `rfc6035_2otel_build_info_ratio`

Phase 2 remains gated until the corrected released build passes every item in Wave 2 section 5.2.
title: fix: preserve the frozen build-info Prometheus series name

## Objective

Remove the SIP observer integration test race exposed by release-PR CI without changing runtime behavior.

## Evidence

CI run 31636885860 at release PR head bd0168b45d8db8f55de9d6eec628d53934b8565a failed TestListenerSurvivesHostileDatagramsAndDeduplicates. The handler count reached one before the concurrent duplicate datagram goroutine recorded its observer events: duplicate:test-phone was 0, response:200 was 1, while accepted was already 2.

## Scope

internal/sip/listener_test.go only. Wait for the asynchronous observer state with a bounded deadline. Do not serialize or alter the production UDP listener.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The focused SIP test passes repeatedly and under -race.
- [ ] Integrated make check passes.
- [ ] Exact-head CI and release-PR CI pass.
title: test: synchronize SIP observer assertions

After the complete Phase 1 gate only, prove at least three completed real calls per handset/dialect plus duplicate suppression and process stability.

## Ownership

## Dependencies
Every one of the seven gate items must pass first.

## Acceptance
- [x] At least three standard reports from PHONE-A and three pre-standard reports from PHONE-B land.
- [x] Replayed identical Call-ID+CSeq increments duplicates without exporting another report.
- [x] RSS before/after and restart count are recorded; restart count remains 0.

comments.body:
## Parked partial — precise resume boundary

The independently executable soak checks passed on released `service_version="0.1.1"`:

- before injection: HOST-A healthy, restart count 0, `VmRSS=24960 kB`, `VmHWM=24960 kB`
- sent the immutable pre-standard capture twice from an in-memory copy, changing only SIP/report identity; both 1,247-byte datagrams received `SIP/2.0 200 OK`
- live `rfc6035_2otel_reports_total{service_version="0.1.1"}` gained exactly one pre-standard report
- live `rfc6035_2otel_duplicates_total{service_version="0.1.1"}` returned exactly 1
- HOST-A log contains exactly one export for call id `wave2-p2-dedupe`
- after injection: healthy, restart count 0, `VmRSS=25012 kB`, `VmHWM=25012 kB`

The real-call criterion is not met. Current live rows contain only sender `unknown`: two controlled standard reports and one controlled pre-standard report. There are zero handset-originated rows labelled `PHONE-A` or `PHONE-B`. The Wave 2 run contract limits phone access to read-only `config/get` and `lineInfo`; remotely originating or hanging up calls would exceed authority, and no human is available mid-run.

Resume at the phones: place and hang up at least three calls whose reports originate from PHONE-A (`standard`) and three whose reports originate from PHONE-B (`prestandard`). Then query `rfc6035_2otel_reports_total{service_version="0.1.1"}` broken down by `rfc6035_sender_name,rfc6035_report_dialect`, confirm at least 3 for each required pairing, re-read RSS/restart count, and close this issue with a completion commit. Do not count the controlled `unknown` replays as real calls.

## Acceptance complete on released 0.1.1

Three real completed calls involved both handsets. The released-service query returned exactly `PHONE-A / standard = 3` and `PHONE-B / prestandard = 3` from `rfc6035_2otel_reports_total{service_version="0.1.1"}`.

The first validation call exposed a deployment omission: HOST-A had no `senders:` block, so its two reports correctly landed as `unknown`. I added only the frozen PHONE-A and PHONE-B mappings to `/opt/rfc6035-2otel/config.yaml`, recreated the same digest-pinned image, and did not count that call toward the named pairing query. The post-recreate baseline was `VmRSS=22328 kB`, `VmHWM=22328 kB`, healthy, restart count 0. The final snapshot was `VmRSS=24580 kB`, `VmHWM=24580 kB`, healthy, restart count 0, with UDP 5060 held by the released process.

The prior controlled replay remains the duplicate proof: exactly one accepted pre-standard report, `rfc6035_2otel_duplicates_total{service_version="0.1.1"} = 1`, and exactly one export log for its call id. No replay was counted as a real handset call.

title: P1-L1: Correct the public metric and log contract

body:
## Mission

Bring rfc6035-2otel from the deployed Wave 1 prototype to sibling parity with polylens2otel, correct the public OpenTelemetry signal contract before it freezes, cut v0.1.0, deploy the CI-published image to HOST-A by digest, and prove the released build live.

Run contract: Phase 1 must complete before the seven-item gate. No Phase 2 entry may start unless the gate passes in full. Root owns GitHub, git, CI, release, HOST-A, Grafana, phones, and integration. Lane workers are local-only and never commit or use networked tools.

## Frozen decisions

- D1: observed-call signals use rfc6035.*; collector self-signals use rfc6035_2otel.*.
- D2: first release is v0.1.0. A future 1.0.0 requires both a non-Poly RFC 6035 sender and the pre-standard grammar from a second Poly model or firmware.
- D3: self-observability, docs/docs-sync, dashboard/alerts, and Helm are all in scope.
- D4: metric sender identity comes only from the bounded operator sender map; unmatched is unknown; raw client address is log-only.
- D5: exactly nine self-signals: build_info, datagrams, reports, parse_errors, duplicates, responses, export_failures, dedupe_cache.usage, and report.process.duration, with the frozen names/units/closed attributes from the Wave 2 goal.
- D6: self dashboard means Grafana panels, never an in-binary HTTP or Prometheus endpoint.
- D7: HOST-A retains network_mode: host.
- D8: HOST-A normalises to /opt/rfc6035-2otel/config.yaml plus /opt/compose/rfc6035-2otel/{compose.yml,.env}, with a digest-pinned GHCR image and no source tree.
- D9: release-please uses permission-set and role release-please-rfc6035-2otel; docs-sync uses permission-set docs-sync and role docs-sync-rfc6035-2otel.
- D10: required workflows are ci, codeql, scorecard, dependency-review, docker-security, actionlint, zizmor, publish, release-please, release-assets, helm, and trigger-docs-sync.
- D11: generated dashboards and rules live in this repository; this run does not write them to Grafana Cloud.
- D12: no credential rotation.
- D13: delay/jitter metrics export seconds; loss/discard metrics export 0–1 ratios with unit 1; logs retain wire milliseconds and percentages.
- D14: explicit histogram boundaries are frozen by family.
- D15: log body is the raw report; event.name is a field only; registry client/network attributes are present.
- D16: the OTel resource merges the standard environment/default resource while explicit service attributes remain authoritative.
- Wave 1 decisions still binding: both dialects auto-detected; UDP only; no syslog; metrics and logs but no traces; Go.
- spec/protocol.md remains binding in full, and real captures outrank the RFC-derived grammar.

## Full rfc6035.* rename contract

| Before | After | Contract detail |
|---|---|---|
| vq.call.mos_lq, vq.call.mos_cq, vq.call.r_factor_lq, vq.call.r_factor_cq | rfc6035.call.* with the same leaves | Prefix change; scores remain unit 1 |
| vq.call.packet_loss, vq.call.discard_rate | rfc6035.call.packet_loss, rfc6035.call.discard_rate | Metric values change from 0–100 percent to 0–1 ratio, unit 1; logs keep wire percent |
| vq.call.round_trip_delay, vq.call.one_way_delay, vq.call.jitter | rfc6035.call.* with the same leaves | Metric values change from milliseconds to seconds, unit s; logs keep wire milliseconds |
| vq.report.dialect, vq.report.type, vq.report.call_id | rfc6035.report.* with the same leaves | call_id remains log-only |
| vq.direction with local/remote | rfc6035.report.side with local/remote | This is endpoint side, not network I/O direction |
| vq.jitter.type with IAJ/MAJ | rfc6035.jitter.kind with interarrival/mean_absolute | Key and values both change |
| vq.field.<x> and vq.field.<x>.original_key | rfc6035.field.<x>; original_key only when it differs from the normalised key | Lossless overflow without redundant attributes |
| log event vq.report.received | rfc6035.report.received | Event-name field, with no duplicate event.name attribute |

Every metric and attribute key is namespaced. Metrics and logs also carry rfc6035.sender.name from the bounded sender map. The raw client address never appears on metrics.

Histogram boundaries:
- MOS: 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 3.5, 3.8, 4, 4.2, 4.4, 5
- R-factor: 0, 20, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 94, 100
- loss/discard: 0, 0.001, 0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1
- delay/jitter seconds: 0.001, 0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5, 1

The log body is the original report text; registry attributes client.address, client.port, network.transport=udp, and network.protocol.name=sip are used; logs preserve wire units. The resource honours OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES and OTEL_SERVICE_NAME and includes telemetry SDK metadata, with explicit service values overriding environment values.

## Entries

- [x] P1-L1 metric contract
- [x] P1-L2 self-observability
- [x] P1-L3 release plumbing
- [x] P1-L4 workflow set
- [x] P1-L5 docs
- [x] P1-L6 dashboard and alerts
- [x] P1-L7 Helm chart
- [x] GATE: all seven gate items
- [x] P2-L8 two-dialect soak
- [x] P2-L9 docs hub
- [x] P2-L10 parser hardening

## Gate

- [x] Integrated make check is green.
- [x] Exact pushed SHA is green in CI, including first CodeQL, Scorecard, zizmor, actionlint, dependency-review, and docker-security executions.
- [x] Release PR is chore(main): release 0.1.0; merge produces v0.1.0, GitHub Release, green publish/binaries, and a public GHCR package.
- [x] HOST-A runs the released digest-pinned image in the normalised layout, healthy with restart count 0 and UDP 5060.
- [x] Released service_version proves rfc6035_* present, vq_* absent, corrected live values/buckets, real build metadata, self-signals, and a raw-report log.

title: Wave 2: sibling parity, public signal contract, and v0.1.0

body:
## Mission

Implement the frozen 2026-08-12 Wave 1 goal: receive live Poly Edge E350 RFC 6035 voice-quality PUBLISH reports in both standard and Poly pre-standard dialects, parse them, export OTLP metrics and logs, and replace the Python collector on HOST-A.

## Binding decisions

- Go; UDP only; both dialects auto-detected.
- Metrics and logs over OTLP; no traces, syslog, or Prometheus endpoint.
- Real captures outrank the RFC-derived field list.
- Root owns package seams, integration, commits, pushes, Lens writes, and HOST-A deployment.
- OPNsense and all Poly Lens attributes except the collector address/port are out of scope.

## Plan

1. Capture a real report from each handset dialect and restore the Lens collector target.
2. Implement the parser, SIP listener, OTLP exporter, and validated YAML/environment configuration in isolated lanes.
3. Wire the packages and run the integrated gate.
4. Build and deploy a hardened host-network container on HOST-A, replacing the Python collector.
5. Prove both signals in Grafana Cloud and record live final state.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Real standard-dialect capture exists, or an explicit not-obtained disposition records why it remains unmeasured.
- [ ] Real pre-standard capture exists, or an explicit not-obtained disposition records why it remains unmeasured.
- [ ] Parser handles both measured dialects, all seven frozen protocol traps, absent values, folding, and unknown fields.
- [ ] SIP listener returns conformant responses, deduplicates retransmissions, and survives hostile datagrams.
- [ ] OTLP metrics and one full-field log record are exported per report; call IDs never become metric attributes.
- [ ] YAML plus environment configuration loads and validates with actionable errors.
- [ ] `make check` passes on the integrated tree.
- [ ] Container is non-root/read-only/cap-drop-all and compose validates.
- [ ] New collector owns UDP 5060 on HOST-A; Python collector container is absent.
- [ ] Grafana Cloud queries return metric and log rows.
- [ ] Poly Lens collector address is restored to `IP-HOST-A:5060` and verified by read-back.
- [ ] Final Wave 1 report is written with all seven lane dispositions and exact evidence.

comments.body:
Wave 1 checkpoint (pre-integration):

- W1 captured a genuine 833-byte standard-dialect PUBLISH from PHONE-A. Two connected/terminated calls from PHONE-B produced no packet at HOST-A; independent phone syslog shows `Publish Vq-Rtcp-Xr` attempts timing out after about 32 seconds, so pre-standard remains explicitly unmeasured rather than inferred. Both handsets read back with collector `IP-HOST-A:5060`; no Lens policy write was made.
- W3 focused SIP suite passes: concurrent UDP handling, conformant status paths, Call-ID+CSeq dedupe, and listener liveness after hostile datagrams.
- W5 focused configuration suite passes after adding the root-owned YAML dependency.
- W2 is now active against the real standard fixture; W4 implementation is correcting current OTel SDK API drift after exact dependency resolution.

No commit yet; W6 integration remains the next commit boundary.

Wave 1 final checkpoint:

- Commit `25f9b4d954be9f7077dd9f07ff2654f4d9db6391` is on `main`; exact-head CI run `31623576736` passed.
- The hardened `rfc6035-2otel:wave1` container is healthy on HOST-A, owns UDP 5060, runs as `65532:65532` with a read-only root filesystem, host networking, all capabilities dropped, and no-new-privileges. The Python `vq-collector` container count is zero.
- A real PHONE-A call produced one 833-byte standard PUBLISH; the Go collector returned `200 OK` with no retransmission, exported 24 metric series, and produced one native OTLP log row. Exact m7kni queries for `vq_call_mos_lq_count{service_name="rfc6035-2otel",vq_report_dialect="standard"}` and `{service_name="rfc6035-2otel"} | vq_report_call_id="b6da229c5a008a2b2040cb32eb139733"` each returned one row.
- PHONE-B again entered `Publish Vq-Rtcp-Xr` for 32 seconds and returned to `Idle`, but a 90-second HOST-A capture saw zero packets from `IP-PHONE-B`. The pre-standard grammar therefore remains unmeasured and is cleanly rejected rather than inferred.
- Both handsets authoritatively read back collector `IP-HOST-A:5060`, session reports enabled, periodic reports disabled, with PHONE-A standard (`1`) and PHONE-B pre-standard (`0`).

The code/deployment outcome is complete for the measured standard path. The frozen both-dialects outcome remains partial solely because the pre-standard handset emits no wire packet; its exact resume boundary is preserved in `testdata/real/prestandard-2026-08-12.not-obtained.md`. The required run-end report is the terminal local action and follows after this tracker update.

Final-head addendum: the parser-owned dialect seam fix is now commit `8763e9c8c17ae8c23eb46ea8253c5cd3631a4bfe`, pushed to `main` with exact-head CI run `31624504916` successful. HOST-A was rebuilt and force-recreated from that head; the healthy container reports the same commit. A fresh PHONE-A call at the final head produced standard report `005cafcee1d48f77e554b233f7139733`; the exact m7kni MOS metric query and exact-call log query each returned one row with `service_version="8763e9c"`. Final live counts remain one new container, zero Python containers, and 29 deployment files.

Pre-standard diagnostic addendum:

- Live `config/get` parity now covers collector address/port, RTCP-XR enable, session/periodic switches, location, alert thresholds, and IPv4 mode. The only intentional VQ difference remains `rfc6035.enable` (`1` PHONE-A, `0` PHONE-B).
- Under the same call procedure, PHONE-A records `CStatePublishClient::OnEvResponse 200`; PHONE-B records `CStatePublishClient::OnEvResponse 480` plus a self-generated PUBLISH timeout after 32 seconds. A simultaneous HOST-A capture still records zero packets from PHONE-B. This narrows the boundary to the handset or a destination selected before HOST-A; it does not reveal a body grammar.
- Read-only Lens `accessPCAPUrl` returned `NO_AVAILABLE_PCAPS`. Starting a new device PCAP was not attempted because Wave 1 did not grant that external mutation.
- The stronger disposition is committed at `ce495686efcdff630a452ccb68f25bf454941486`; exact-head CI run `31625260683` passed. The healthy HOST-A implementation remains `8763e9c` because this final commit changes documentation only.

Resume requires separate authority for a Lens device PCAP, physical Ethernet/LAN access to PHONE-B, or the attempted PUBLISH from the selected SIP proxy. Until one produces a real packet, pre-standard grammar remains deliberately unimplemented.

Firewall-unblock completion addendum:

- Rob added the narrowly scoped IOT-to-HOST-A exception. The agent did not access or change OPNsense.
- A genuine pre-standard PUBLISH from PHONE-B was captured and committed as testdata/real/prestandard-2026-08-12.txt. The measured body uses a bare VQSessionReport line plus paired ToID/FromID fields; the parser now detects that structural pair and maps it to the common call-identity model.
- Final implementation commit 206c6f1f01137a934462f8218cac98b6165f9cf6 is pushed on main. Exact-head CI run 31628098859, job 94219659972, passed go vet, go test -race, go mod tidy -diff, and the production build.
- HOST-A is running the same final commit in healthy image rfc6035-2otel:wave1. The process owns UDP 5060, runs as 65532:65532 with read-only rootfs, host networking, all capabilities dropped, and no-new-privileges. Final live counts are one new container, zero Python containers, and 30 deployment files.
- PHONE-B final-head call 8fbf6990b15d8914e46f71e84c908b97 produced one pre-standard PUBLISH and one 200 OK with no retransmission in the 90-second capture. The exact m7kni metric query for service_version=206c6f1 and vq_report_dialect=prestandard returned one row/value 1; the exact-call log query returned one row with dialect prestandard and client_address IP-PHONE-B.
- PHONE-A final-head call f78e97cab264e550e5d9b4b12b139733 exported as standard. Its exact m7kni metric query for service_version=206c6f1 and vq_report_dialect=standard returned one row/value 1; the exact-call log query returned one row with dialect standard and client_address IP-PHONE-A.
- Final authoritative config/get read-back shows both phones targeting IP-HOST-A:5060 with RTCP-XR and session reports enabled and periodic reports disabled. PHONE-A remains standard mode (rfc6035.enable=1); PHONE-B remains pre-standard mode (rfc6035.enable=0). No Lens policy write occurred, so no restoration mutation was required.

All W1-W7 acceptance outcomes are now satisfied at the final head. The terminal report will preserve the distinction between local, exact-head CI, deployed, and live/Grafana proof.
